title: Fractions: comparing equal-sized parts
subtitle: Compare fractions by describing them with equal-sized parts.
challenge: Two cylinders of equal capacity are filled to 3/4 and 5/8 of their volumes. Which cylinder contains more liquid?
predictionPrompt: Make a prediction: Is 3/4 smaller than, equal to, or greater than 5/8?
formalDefinition: For nonnegative whole numbers a and positive whole numbers b, a/b means a copies of the part 1/b. A common denominator rewrites two fractions using equal-sized parts of the same whole.

steps: Find the least common multiple of 4 and 8: lcm(4, 8) = 8.
Convert 3/4 by multiplying numerator and denominator by 2: (3×2)/(4×2) = 6/8.

misconception.mistake: Since 5 > 3 and 8 > 4, 5/8 must be greater than 3/4.
misconception.correction: Fractions cannot be compared by numerators alone when part sizes differ. Each eighth is half the size of a fourth.

reflection: To compare two rational numbers a/b and c/d, scale both to a common denominator D = lcm(b, d) and compare the integer numerators.
prerequisiteCheck: A fraction compares equal-sized parts of the same whole. Explain why 1/2 and 2/4 mark the same point before comparing fractions.
representation: Draw two equal-length strips. Split the first into 4 equal parts and shade 3; split the second into 8 and shade 5. Splitting each fourth in half produces 6 shaded eighths without changing the first strip.

faded.solution: 2/3 = 8/12 and 3/4 = 9/12, so 2/3 < 3/4. Every piece now has the same size.

independent.prompt: Compare 4/6 and 2/3. What case did the first worked example not include?
independent.solution: They are equal: 4/6 simplifies to 2/3. Comparison must include equality, not just less/greater.

explanation: Explain why multiplying both numerator and denominator by the same positive integer preserves the fraction. Your explanation should refer to subdividing parts or multiplying by 1.

transfer.prompt: Bottle A contains 3/4 of a 1-litre bottle. Bottle B contains 5/8 of a 2-litre bottle. Which holds more liquid? Why does the original comparison no longer decide?
transfer.solution: A contains 3/4 litre; B contains 10/8 = 5/4 litres. B holds more. Fraction comparisons describe equal wholes only when the whole units match.

retrieval: Tomorrow, without reopening the example, compare 7/12 and 3/5. A week later, compare 5/8 and 2/3 and explain why your method is valid.
